note: Attacker-controlled bytes from UART are copied into the CLI receive buffer.
The receive buffer is passed to the CLI interpreter for parsing.
The input string is split into arguments; argv[0]="service", argv[1]="add", argv[2]=enterprise_number, argv[3]=service_data, argv[4]=server_data.
The length of the service data argument is cast to uint8_t, allowing values 253-255 even though the destination buffer is only 252 bytes.
memcpy copies up to 255 bytes into a 252-byte stack buffer, causing a stack-based buffer overflow.
